notes: Rule 3 sanity check passed: genuine Zara Home / Inditex site (ZARA HOME branding throughout, 'ZARA HOME FILIALEN' store locator, ZARA HOME BUSINESS section), no closing-down language, storefront live and selling. DE storefront (https://www.zarahome.com/de/) confirmed as a GENUINELY SEPARATE Inditex catalogue from both S.N. 21 Zara Home UAE and S.N. 98 Zara Home UK: store 84009904 / catalog 80290000 (vs UK's 84009906/80290024 and UAE's 85009931/50333562), EUR pricing, languageId -3 / de-DE, countryCode DE confirmed in embedded appconfig. Independently re-verified the same distinct-population pattern the UK worker found: DE's 'Bedroom Mirrors' node resolves to the identical internal categoryId 1020241660 that UK also used for its own Bedroom Mirrors row, but returns 13 products under DE's store/catalog vs UK's 12 -- same taxonomy ID, different per-country population, exactly as expected on this shared Inditex platform. However most other leaf categories on DE map to their OWN distinct internal categoryId (e.g. DE Table Lamps = categoryId 1020692630 vs UK's 1020447640) -- the shared element across countries is the SEO url-suffix ('-nNNNN', a redirect-layer id), not the internal catalog categoryId, and DE/UK/UAE each have their own catalog populations. Access route: Akamai Bot Manager JS interstitial solved once per session with pipeline/final_list_batch_sn21-30/inditex_interstitial_solver.py's proof-of-work logic unmodified (curl_cffi chrome impersonation, de-DE Accept-Language), then cookies reused directly for the rest of the session with no per-request re-solve needed. Category discovery: DE's static SSR nav/footer HTML only exposes a partial slug list; the full set of UK-equivalent leaf/parent SEO ids (the '-nNNNN' suffixes, which the UK worker's own JSON already enumerates) were tested directly against the DE domain as 302 redirects (nonsense-slug-plus-real-id requests all redirect to DE's own canonical German slug), confirming every UK/AE category node also exists on DE except Borosilicate (n4205), which 404s to /de/error.html and has zero 'borosilikat' mentions anywhere in DE's rendered nav/homepage -- treated as a genuine catalogue absence on this storefront (real answer per Rule 3 discipline), not a broken link; DE's Tumblers/Glasses/Bottles-and-Jugs subtree covers the rest of Glassware. Each leaf qty is the productIds array length from /itxrest/3/catalog/store/84009904/80290000/category/<id>/product?showProducts=false&showNoStock=false&withSubCategories=false&languageId=-3&appId=1 (categoryId extracted from the product-detail deep-links embedded in each category page's own SSR payload), independently re-read twice in two full separate passes (all 35 leaf values and all internal categoryIds identical both times -- no drift). DE renders no 'N items' header anywhere, matching UK/AE; qty is the exact server-rendered grid productIds count, the same method validated on S.N. 21 and S.N. 98. RULE 0: included Bathroom Lighting (beleuchtung-lampen-bad-n5792, qty 5) and Bathroom Mirrors (badezimmer-spiegel-n2468, qty 11), which a room-word exclusion would have wrongly dropped, plus Kids Lamps and Lighting (kinder-schlafzimmer-lampen-n1117, qty 17) and Bedroom Lamps (schlafzimmer-beleuchtung-n966, qty 41), all real decorative-lighting room branches. 'Mirrors' landing (dekoration-spiegel-wohnzimmer-n993, categoryId 1089523, 40 products) is treated as the parent grouping node, matching UK's treatment of the same node; its child listings carry the counts. 'Lamps and Lighting' landing (beleuchtung-lampen-n4847, categoryId 1020692635, 95 products) is likewise the parent grouping node for Lighting, matching UK. 'Hooks' (categoryId 1090528, kleiderhaken-n4857, German label literally 'Kleiderhaken' = Clothing Hooks, qty 17) is kept as a genuinely separate decorative-hooks node from 'Door knobs and handles' (categoryId 1020447447, knaufe-turgriffe-n1005, qty 43, hardware): product-ID overlap check showed only 14 of Hooks' 17 products inside Door-knobs-and-handles' 43, confirming the latter is a mixed hardware/decor rollup, exactly the 14/17-vs-UK's-15/18 pattern -- kept Hooks, dropped Door-knobs-and-handles.
